findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 2 ('CI asserts the bijection...')

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the marker retire/cleanup rule (a marker is removed when its ADR is deleted/renamed) so the bijection check stays green.

No statement about what happens to a marker when an ADR is removed/renamed
findings.finding: The .numbers/NNNN marker files are new shared state, but the plan does not define a RETIRE path: when an ADR is deleted or superseded, is its marker removed, and does the CI bijection check then fail? Lifecycle create/consume are covered (AC1/AC2) but retirement is unspecified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the 'no two markers share content' assertion is a non-race-free check-then-act (unlike the path-collision guarantee) and either accept the residual explicitly (with rationale, e.g. content collisions are rare and mapping is human-authored) or add a mechanism that makes content collisions produce a git conflict too.
evidence: The path-collision guarantee only fires for the SAME number: two markers on DIFFERENT numbers (e.g. 0092 and 0093) that both name the same ADR filename occupy different paths and produce NO git conflict.

Plan quote grounding the concern: 'A pre-merge uniqueness check on a monotonic counter is racy by construction, and ADR 0047 explicitly accepts that a change may land without re-running CI after a server-side rebase.' — the content-uniqueness assertion is exactly that kind of racy pre-merge check.

ADR 0047 Decision 1 accepts that a change may land 'without re-running integration CI' after a non-conflicted rebase, so two concurrent changes that each pass the content-uniqueness check on their own base can both land.
findings.finding: The AC-2 'no two markers share content' assertion is only a check-then-act CI check, not protected by the race-free add/add mechanism, so it retains the same TOCTOU exposure the plan rejects for a monotonic counter.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 2 ('CI asserts the bijection ... and that no two markers share content'); Prevention section
scenarios: Two authors on stale bases each add distinct-numbered ADRs whose markers accidentally reference the same filename; both pass CI locally; both land without a git conflict, defeating the content-uniqueness invariant.

The plan does not say where the bijection check lives (a new script vs. extending check_docs_index.py) or how the generated ADR index relates to the existing docs/README.md index the checker already governs
findings.finding: The plan adds a new generated docs/adr/README.md index and a new CI bijection/uniqueness check without stating whether they extend the repo's existing docs-index tooling or stand up parallel machinery — a potential NIH / duplicate-check-surface risk.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria lines 2-3 ('CI asserts the bijection...'; 'A generated docs/adr/README.md index exists')
scenarios: Implementer writes a fresh adr-index generator + a standalone uniqueness script when check_docs_index.py could be extended to cover docs/adr/, splitting index-integrity logic across two tools

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a short prior-art note reconciling the bespoke tooling with the established ADR ecosystem: state whether adr-tools (or similar) was considered for number allocation and README/TOC generation, and why the marker-file mechanism must be bespoke (existing tools don't address the Gerrit stale-base / rebase-without-CI race per ADR 0047).
evidence: Plan proposes 'A generated docs/adr/README.md index' and per-number marker files but never references existing ADR tooling.

Retrieved prior art: npryce/adr-tools (github.com/npryce/adr-tools) is the de-facto CLI for managing ADRs incl. numbering and index; ADR guides (Fowler bliki, adr.github.io) treat monotonic numbering + README index as standard practice.

The plan strongly justifies the NOVEL part (marker-file add/add conflict vs racy CI check vs shared index at ~23% spurious conflict) — but the non-novel index/allocation surfaces are presented as bespoke without a prior-art note.
findings.finding: The plan builds bespoke ADR tooling (marker generation, CI bijection check, generated README index) without considering the established ADR tooling ecosystem (e.g. npryce/adr-tools) as prior art for number allocation and index/TOC generation. The novel git-conflict uniqueness mechanism is well-justified against alternatives, but the overlapping index-generation and number-allocation surfaces are not reconciled with existing tools.
findings.location: Plan body 'Prevention is git's, not CI's' + Acceptance Criteria (README index / marker generation)
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks why README index generation and number allocation were hand-rolled rather than delegated to adr-tools, which already generates a TOC and allocates the next number.
findings.suggested_fix: In 'Prevention is git's, not CI's', add: 'Existing ADR tooling (npryce/adr-tools) allocates numbers and generates a TOC but relies on a monotonic counter that does not survive the Gerrit stale-base race (16 of 22 collisions) nor ADR 0047's land-without-CI-after-rebase; hence the bespoke .numbers/NNNN marker. Index generation follows standard ADR practice (Fowler / adr.github.io).'
